body: tests-tool-owns-the-per-test-run-loop: The record's narrative, options, and recommendation still match the code, but its line links have rotted; relink them. Evidence: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:cmd_run now sits at L1398 (filed L994) and builds the targets, then runs `results = [run_one(root, testing, sid, test) for sid, test in targets]` at L1414 (filed L1010); run_one at L1347 (filed L943) starts one shell process per test with a per-test timeout; command_for at L1340 (filed L936) fills {path} and {name} into testing.run. The round line is appended to the sprint's -results.jsonl only at L1422, after every run_one returns, so an interrupted round records nothing. The --from-file path still runs one process per entry. Mechanism: one process per test reruns session-scoped setup for every test and serializes the suite. Corpus: decision:scenario-list-decided-once commits 'The project declares how one test runs as `testing.run` in its configuration, a command holding `{path}` and, where the runner needs it, `{name}`'; options A and B amend that sentence, C keeps it. decision:test-support-written-before-tests and decision:tests-check-scenarios are silent on how a round runs. The owner's own words (quoted in the problem) settle that the project, not the suite, owns the loop, which rules out C on the owner's terms, but leave A versus B open. Options as filed stand with their costs; one cost the filer missed for A: the suite must define what a test's result line names (scenario id or path and name) so the tool can match a project runner's output to the scenario list, and a test the runner never reports must read as failed, not passed. No accept-list entry is needed: this is a judgment issue about the project's own tooling. Rule together with plan-tests-declares-the-runner-before-planning (route question), which also changes what /plan-tests asks the owner to declare about the runner and offers a per-kind command (its option B) that interacts with A here.

owner-list-refiles-closed-judgments: Evidence re-verified. The /converge owner-list prompt (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/owner-list.md) reads only open issues before filing: L15 names `issues list --json` 'prints every open issue'; the dedupe steps at L23 ('read `issues list --category defect --json` for an open issue at the same site'), L32, L42, and L61 ('read `issues list --json` for an open issue on the same ...') check open issues alone; L83 says the module 'refuses an id already open', so a closed id can be filed again. Neither merge.md nor the triage prompt reads .ok-planner/history/issues.jsonl. Mechanism: closing an issue moves its record to the archive, so every later writer's dedupe misses it, and the next run that meets the same harm or question files it fresh. Corpus: decision:intake-writers-are-gated says 'Deduplication against the slugs already present is the standing discipline of every writer into the intake, the gates included'; 'already present' does not say whether the archive counts, so the corpus does not settle this. story:find-and-fix-defects promises the owner meets 'only the questions that need my judgment'; concept:issue and decision:foreign-harms-become-upstream-issues define closing as moving to the archive and say nothing on refiling. Harm: owner attention spent judging a closed question again; no accept-list entry needed for a judgment issue. Options: A (keep open-only dedupe, amend story:find-and-fix-defects to say a closed question returns): cheapest, and it narrows the story's promise. B (dedupe against the archive too, amend decision:intake-writers-are-gated): stops the repeats, and it must say when a closed question may reopen. An option the filer missed, C: dedupe against the archive only for issues closed as retired or answered by the owner (judgment closes), and never against issues closed fixed or promoted, so a regression of a fixed defect still files; cost: the decision must name which close kinds suppress a refile and what new evidence reopens one. Note under B and C that a refiled id collides with nothing today, so the writer, not the module, would carry the check unless the module learns to refuse an archived id. Recommend ruling it alone; no sibling open issue covers intake dedupe.

body: workflow-drain-marks-stages-only-on-return: Evidence, re-verified, still holds. The drain's Workflow form returns only on done, waiting, stuck, paused (950 agents), or failed (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_tasks/drain.md:16-22); a chained next stage becomes ready inside the same script run, so a sprint whose stages chain returns once, at the end. Sprint step 6 (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:159-167) marks every entry in progress when the drain that runs its build task starts, and done when the task closes; under the Workflow form the session learns of closes only on return. Mechanism: the session marks entries; the session wakes once per drain by design, so no entry turns done until the script returns. Corpus: story:watch-execution-progress promises stages 'each marked as it lands, so that I can follow a long run without opening the completion report'. decision:task-tools-mirror-the-report, amended by the sprint now in the tree, says 'Where a Workflow script runs the drain, the session marks each entry from the closed tasks the script returns, each time it returns.' decision:drain-runs-as-a-workflow-script says 'The session wakes once per drain and acts on what the script returns', with the rationale that each wake rereads the whole context (967,000 tokens, three compactions in 370 tasks). The two decisions and the drain text agree; the story contradicts them. Harm: display only; the report and run file stay the record. No accept-list entry is needed for a judgment issue. Options: (A) mark as each stage lands: amend drain-runs-as-a-workflow-script so the script also returns when a stage's key closes, costing one session wake per stage (far fewer than one per agent, more than one per drain), and amend task-tools-mirror-the-report to match; (B) mark on return: amend story:watch-execution-progress to promise entries marked each time the drain returns, keeping the one-wake drain and losing a live view of chained stages; (C, filer missed) have the Workflow script's own step agents update the harness checklist as tasks close, if the harness lets a script-started agent write the session's task list: no extra wake, but it depends on a harness capability nothing in the tree confirms. A corpus-route reading exists (the decision delta is the later approved text and the code matches it), but option B narrows a story promise, so the owner chooses. Siblings: none in this batch.

approved-test-sprint-across-true-up-boundary: Evidence, re-verified, still holds. .ok-planner/release-boundaries.md (Trued-up projects) says 'Not across it: a sprint, documentation sprint, or test sprint in execution, and a planning run in progress. The owner trues up only between them, never while one is being planned or executed, and a sprint runs soon after it is planned.' Its 'What crosses it' list names 'sprints' among the owner's records the estate holds, without naming test sprints. The sprint now in the tree adds plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:plan_folders (tests:255-258), which raises 'the plan records no folders: assemble it again with ' for a plan with no folders list; a plan an earlier release approved has none. True-up skips test sprints as records (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/ADMINISTRATION.md:308) and migrates none. Mechanism: an approved, unstarted test sprint sits between planning and execution, the state the boundary text lets the owner true up in, yet the text names only runs in execution or planning as not across. Corpus: concept:release-boundary ('Stored state is always one'); decision:release-boundaries-bind-changes ('Every planned change and every fix keeps each user across a boundary working unless a ruling allows otherwise'). Neither says whether an approved unstarted sprint is stored state across the boundary. The file to amend is the project's own .ok-planner/release-boundaries.md (no suite stamp). Options: (A) left out: amend the boundary to say an approved sprint of any kind runs on the release that planned it and the owner trues up only after it closes; cost: an owner who trues up early must replan the test sprint, and the refusal's message already says how; (B) across: name an approved, unstarted test sprint as across, so the tests tool reads a plan with no folders list (for example as the project's declared folders) or true-up migrates it; cost: a compatibility path in tests or true-up, and the same question then binds sprints and documentation sprints; (C, filer missed) across for all three kinds of approved sprint, consistent with 'sprints' already listed under What crosses it; widest cost. Under B or C, release-boundaries-bind-changes then makes the tests change a defect of the sprint in the tree. Siblings: none in this batch.

drive-prompt-forbids-undoing-scratch-probe-edits: Evidence, re-verified, still holds. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/drive.md:70 reads 'Run any command that may write against a scratch copy of the project or a scratch project of your own, never at the project root. ... Mechanism: the ban protects uncommitted work at the root; a driver is the one agent that writes, and only in scratch, so the ban also forbids undoing its own scratch edits. Corpus: decision:drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user says 'A driver changes nothing in the project's tree: a command that may write runs against a scratch copy or a scratch project, never at the project root'; it is silent on git verbs inside scratch. .ok-planner/review/project.md 'What no agent of this loop ever runs' does not name these verbs. The change edits the product's own prompt source, drive.md (the project owns it; .claude/skills/ holds the suite's materialized copy). No stated rule decides the change. Options: (A) scope the ban to the project root and allow the verbs in a scratch project of the driver's own; cost: a scratch copy made with `git worktree add` shares refs and the stash list with the root repository, so `stash` and a branch-moving `checkout` or `reset` there reach the root; the scope must say a repository the driver made with `git init` or a full copy, never a worktree; (B) keep the ban whole and tell a driver to make a fresh scratch project to undo a probe edit; cost: repeats setup such as a true-up per undo; (C, the filer's B second half, the cheapest) keep the ban and tell a driver to copy a file aside before a probe edit and copy it back to undo; cost: the driver must plan its undo before the edit. body: legacy-sort-deletes-unwritten-rule-tests: Evidence, re-verified, still holds. The sort agent's table at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/core.md:505-506 ({{TEST-SORT-PROMPT}}) ports a test only where 'It enforces a written rule on the code's shape, such as a module boundary or a naming rule', and deletes 'as an orphan' a test that checks 'a behavior no story or rule names'. core.md:490-493 limits the written rules to the decisions, the practices, .ok-planner/release-boundaries.md, and the rules files under .claude/rules/. No step records a call or files an issue for a test whose rule is unwritten; the deletion only reaches the completion report's veto list. Mechanism: a project adopting the suite has few written rules, so a fitness test enforcing an unwritten layering or naming rule falls to the orphan row, is deleted, and nothing checks the rule afterward. Corpus: story:retire-a-legacy-suite promises the old suite does not 'leave a rule it enforced unchecked' (no 'written' qualifier). decision:legacy-suites-sorted-automatically ports 'A test that enforces a written rule on the code's shape', deletes 'a behavior no story or rule names' as an orphan, and sorts 'without asking the owner about any one test'; its rationale says 'A rule a fitness check enforced still needs a check after the test goes'. decision:tests-check-scenarios: 'A test that checks no live scenario is an orphan'. The story and the decision cannot both hold for an unwritten rule, so the owner chooses. Harm: a rule the old suite enforced goes unchecked (the story's broken promise); no accept-list entry is needed for a judgment issue. Options: (A) narrow story:retire-a-legacy-suite to promise a check for each rule the project has written down; cost: the old suite's unwritten rules can vanish silently, the very loss the story names. (B) amend decision:legacy-suites-sorted-automatically so a test enforcing an unwritten rule on the code's shape raises one question to the owner, who writes the rule down (then the test ports) or lets it go; cost: breaks the decision's 'no question per test' choice, and a fitness-heavy legacy suite can raise many questions. (C, filer missed) amend the decision so the sort ports such a test anyway, naming the rule it infers, and records the inferred rule as a call the owner vetoes in the completion report, with the plan's port task also drafting the rule for a later /plan-sprint practice delta; cost: agents infer rules, and a check enforces a rule no document states until a sprint writes it. (D, filer missed) amend the decision so the sort groups the unwritten-rule tests and files one judgment issue per inferred rule, not per test, holding those tests (kept as written) until the owner writes or drops the rule; cost: legacy tests outlive the first test sprint, and a kept suite blocks removals its tests import, which the decision's alternatives reject. A change under B, C, or D also edits the sort prompt at core.md:490-506 and the plan-tests assembly in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests. Siblings: file-level-runner-sorts-legacy-files-whole, test-sort-decides-fixtures-before-adoptions (same sort, defect issues); ported-check-may-start-a-test-runner (the port path).
